public_rationale: Contemporaneous reporting describes a CoreWeave 2032 bond yield touching 15% on October 13. A separate summary attributed to FINRA TRACE reports 14.7% for the 2031 notes that day, consistent with the claim's whole-percentage precision. This supports the yield observation. It does not establish that credit markets generally stopped financing AI; Marcus presents that broader conclusion as a suggestion.
limitations: The decisive 15% report relies on an investor's chart; direct primary trading records were not obtained.
The evidence does not verify the embedded post's more precise 15.1% figure.
Support applies to the measurable yield claim, not a categorical claim about all credit markets.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: CoreWeave bonds have reached 15%, which suggests that credit markets have had enough.
conditions: 'had enough' is presented as what the bond level suggests, not as an established fact

statement.excerpt: P.S. In other news, early generative AI darling Character.AI has filed for bankruptcy, and Coreweave bonds have reached 15%, suggesting that credit markets have had enough.
statement.document_title: It remains “very difficult [to find] actual, materially measurable financial impacts” from spending on AI, per new study

from_speaker: suggesting that credit markets have had enough
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading of 15% is a secondary-market bond yield, expressed as an annual rate, rather than a coupon, bond price, or credit spread.
The claim means at least one CoreWeave bond reached approximately 15%; it does not require every issue to have that yield.
The whole-percentage figure permits ordinary rounding to 15%. An intraday high qualifies because Marcus says 'have reached', rather than specifying a closing yield.
The embedded October 13 market post and October 14 publication establish the target period as October 13–14, 2026.
The estimate basis reflects the third-party market commentary cited in the post. Currency is null because the asserted yield is a percentage and Marcus specifies no currency.
'Suggesting that credit markets have had enough' is a hedged interpretation of the yield. It is not treated as a separate firm assertion that all credit became unavailable.
criteria.support_condition: Dated market data or reliable reporting establishes that a CoreWeave bond's secondary-market yield reached approximately 15% during October 13–14, 2026.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable coverage of the relevant issues and intraday trading establishes that none reached approximately 15%, or a substantiated correction establishes that the cited figure was not a CoreWeave bond yield.
